method: Split conformal prediction on spatial (leave-districts-out) out-of-fold errors of the share model, 4 bins by predicted value, target coverage 80%. Range = prediction +/- bin half-width, clipped to 0..1. Grid, solar and unserved are bounded separately, so the three ranges do not sum to 1.
coverage_check: Nested spatial coverage: grid 81%, solar 80%, unserved 80%
labels: Rwanda DHS 2025 (DHS-8), restricted data. Only model-derived outputs are published.
feature_sources: population: WorldPop/GP/100m/pop (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; built_up_surface: JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_BUILT_S (2020) [CC BY 4.0]; night_lights_bm: NASA/VIIRS/002/VNP46A2 (Black Marble) median 2024-01-01 to 2026-01-01 [NASA open data, cite Black Marble (confirm)]; travel_time_city: Oxford/MAP/accessibility_to_cities_2015_v1_0 [CC BY 4.0]; travel_time_health: projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/accessibility_to_healthcare/2019 [CC BY 4.0]; slope: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 (ee.Terrain.slope on 100 m mean elevation) [Public domain]; elevation: USGS/SRTMGL1_003 [Public domain]
limitations: Modelled estimate from 560 survey clusters, not a census. Training label is the MAIN lighting source (DHS hv262), so households using grid plus solar count as grid. DHS cluster locations are displaced by up to 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural). Solar versus unserved is separated less well than grid versus non-grid. Night lights and satellite layers cannot see small solar systems. Unserved here is mostly torch users (about 26% nationally), not the official access gap (about 12%). The range is calibrated on cluster-level errors, which include household sampling noise (about 25 households per cluster) and GPS displacement, so it is wider than the uncertainty of the true cell share. Coverage holds on average across districts, not for every cell.
title: High end of the 80% range for the unserved share, 1 km
